notes.title: V1.5.5 — The One Where Permissions Stop Taking Up Half Your Screen
notes.description: The Roles & Permissions page went on a diet. Categories now display as a compact grid instead of a scrollable novel. Toggle actions with a single click, bulk-set entire categories with one button, and see everything at a glance. Your scroll wheel sends its regards.

notes.title: Sidebar Sections: Now With More Sections
notes.description: Added 'Project Detail Tabs' to the sidebar access controls because apparently people wanted to control who sees what inside a project. Also aligned all sections to match the actual sidebar order, which — believe it or not — was not the case before. Nobody noticed. We noticed. It's fixed.

notes.title: Permission Entities: The Census Is Complete
notes.description: Added Excel Updates, Database Migration, My Work, MS Sync, and Project Tagging to the permission system. Previously these features were like the wild west — everyone could access them, nobody could be stopped. Law and order has been restored.

notes.title: Version Check: You Can't Outrun Updates Anymore
notes.description: When we publish a new version, everyone gets logged out automatically. No more 'but it worked on my session from last Tuesday.' Fresh login, fresh version, fresh start. Your cached auth tokens have been given a retirement date.

notes.title: My Work Task Board: Now Actually Counts Things
notes.description: Filter tabs used to show '0' for everything because someone forgot to initialise the counter keys. Notifications and MS 365 action items now appear with proper source badges. The Task Board can finally count to potato.

notes.title: Teams Chat: No Longer a Dead End
notes.description: The sidebar link to Teams Chat was pointing to a simplified page that did approximately nothing useful. Now it goes to the full two-tab experience with Activity and Chat. The old page is still technically alive, like a appendix — present but purposeless.

notes.title: Easter Egg: Still Undiscovered
notes.description: At this point we're starting to wonder if anyone even looks. It's fine. It'll wait. It has nowhere to be.
